issues.description: The problem statement and the template code refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon (declared in the UML and used in Main), but the solution implements the same functionality under a different static name receiveDelivery(String, int, int). Specifically: problem_statement.md declares the SealSaloon API including acceptSupplyDelivery (lines 27-33); the template Main.java calls shop.acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java line 20); the solution's SealSaloon.java defines a static method receiveDelivery(...) (src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java line 47). This naming mismatch will cause calls or tests that expect acceptSupplyDelivery to fail to compile or run against the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's static receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) method to acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity), or add a new static acceptSupplyDelivery method that delegates to receiveDelivery. Ensure the method signature (parameter order and types) and static-ness match the problem statement and example usage so template examples and tests compile and run with the reference solution.
